title: Introduce heuristic cost sampler and epochal workload dashboard for token-cost attribution
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Long-tail token-cost variance is causing noisy SLO alerts for enterprise tenants. Existing token sampling captures high-cost outliers but misses systematic epochal shifts when traffic shape changes (e.g., nightly batch jobs or A/B rollout cohorts). This PR introduces a lightweight heuristic cost sampler and an epochal workload dashboard to make attribution and alert tuning actionable. Summary of changes: 1) heuristic cost sampler: new sampler that combines token-cost weight, recent frequency sketch, and kernel-latency indicator to pick representative invocations for tracing and payload capture; sampler is pluggable into the existing invocation-sampler interface and defaults to a conservative 0.2% sample rate with adaptive bumping when epochal drift is detected; 2) epochal workload dashboard: Grafana dashboard (observability/epochal-cost.json) with epoch cohorting panels, cost delta waterfall, sampled invocation anchors, and a new 'epoch drift' sparkline; 3) alert tiling: alert rules updated to use epoch-aware baselines and an exponential smoothing parameter to reduce churn during planned rollouts (alert rules updated: alerts/token-cost-slo and alerts/long-tail-noise); 4) lightweight replay harness: add a synthetic epochal replay used in CI smoke to validate sampler bump behavior across 3 simulated epochs; 5) unit and integration tests: sampler logic covered with fuzzed distributions and deterministic replay tests; 6) docs: docs/observability/heuristic-sampler.md explains configuration knobs, tradeoffs, and migration steps. Checklist: - [x] Design review with ENG-obs (notes linked in Linear ENG-1428) - [x] Local unit tests - [x] Integration smoke test with synthetic replay - [x] Load-smoke on staging for 24h - [x] Dashboard review with SRE and Product Changes to runtime/config: - new config block observability.sampler.heuristic with fields: enabled (bool), base_rate (float), epoch_window_seconds (int), bump_policy (enum: conservative/aggressive), kernel_latency_threshold_ms (int). Backwards compatible: sampler defaults to disabled unless enabled via config; existing sampling paths unchanged until enabled in cluster config. Rollout plan: staged rollout via canary on dedicated capacity: enable sampler=false by default; enable on 1% of tenants for 48h, monitor drift detector, then ramp to 25% and 100% with SRE approval. Observability acceptance criteria: 1) no increase in error rates or CPU >2% on serving runtime in canary; 2) show reduction in alert noise (fewer distinct alert groups) for test tenants; 3) sampled traces should include high-fidelity kernel-latency and cost attribution tags for downstream debugging. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: additional I/O from sampled invocation capture. Mitigation: sampling rate conservative, sampler attaches only compact digest by default; full payload capture feature gated behind a tenant opt-in. - Risk: mis-calibrated bump policy causing alert suppression. Mitigation: bump policy has strict upper bound and can be overridden per-tenant. Related work: this complements existing epochal and cohort-based PRs (see ENG-1502, PRs linked in Linear).

review_comments: Lucas Ortega: Can you explain why kernel-latency is included in the heuristic? Concerned about correlation with noisy GPU metrics.

Maya Patel: Kernel-latency is a proxy for backend contention; empirical tests on staging showed it identifies invocations where token-cost attribution spans are longer and more informative. Added comments and a unit test that simulates kernel spikes.
Priya Nair: Please add a safety cap to bump_policy to avoid sampling >5% automatically. Also request an e2e smoke run on dedicated-1.
Maya Patel: Added strict upper bound and updated the smoke config for dedicated-1. Ran 24h smoke, metrics attached in CI artifacts.
Evan Brooks: LGTM after minor nits about naming and one additional test for epoch window edge-case.
Maya Patel: Addressed naming nits and added edge-case test for exactly-boundary epoch windows.
release_notes: Add heuristic invocation sampler (opt-in) and epochal workload dashboard to improve token-cost attribution and reduce alert noise. Configurable bump_policy and smoothing to tune alert churn. Backwards compatible; feature off by default.
post_merge_notes: Deployed to staging and canary. SRE to track ENG-1428 metric dashboard widgets for next two weeks. If alert noise does not improve after ramp, revert via feature flag.
